articles.title: The AirPods Max 2 are a great sequel, but not an ambitious one
articles.summary: Apple’s over-ear headphones get the H2 chip and a new built-in amp for better sound and ANC along with new features, but they’re still heavy and expensive.
articles.body: It’s been over five years since the original AirPods Max came out. A minor hardware update in 2024 brought new colors and changed the Lightning port to USB-C (to meet EU regulations), and an update last year added lossless audio and ultra-low latency. But a new version was still well overdue. The $549 AirPods Max 2 sound incredible thanks to a new built-in amp, the internal chip has been upped from the H1 to the H2, and noise-canceling performance competes against the best Sony and Bose have to offer. But the AirPods Max 2 are an upgrade, not a reimagining. They look identical to the first-gen AirPods Max, and have many of the same problems. The H2 chip, which debuted with the AirPods Pro 2 in 2022, brings new features to the Max 2, like adaptive audio, conversation awareness, and live translation. But they’re heavy, they don’t have a power button, and the case is still terrible and doesn’t offer much protection. [Product: Apple AirPods Max (second-gen) | The 40-millimeter drivers are the same from the original AirPods Max, but they now are driven by an improved high dynamic range amplifier, and the new Max 2 are better for it. The bass is full with good definition, so when music extends into deep low frequencies — like “bury a friend” by Billie Eilish — you can make out the tonality of those notes instead of them sounding boomy or splatty. They might be a bit bass-heavy for some, but I enjoyed the low-end oomph the AirPods Max 2 provided with pop / rock and orchestral tracks alike. And the bass doesn’t overwhelm the upper frequencies, instead supporting them as it should. Midrange vocals and instruments are easily delineated and sound present without sticking out too much. The opening French horn during Brahms’ “Piano Concerto No. 2” with Emil Gilels sounds rich and warm leading into Gilels’ piano response. And when the orchestra hits the main theme full force, the strings, woodwinds, brass, and timpani washed over me, causing me to forget I was writing a review as I sat back to listen. The Max 2 also support lossless audio at 24-bit / 48kHz when using a USB-C-to-USB-C cable (this was a part of the 2025 AirPods Max update, but wasn’t available on the Lightning version). The AirPods Max 2 integrate easily into the Apple ecosystem, as do all Apple products, with fast pairing, Siri interactions with head gestures, auto switching between Apple devices, and spatial audio. The H2 chip had capability ahead of its time, and in the past few years Apple has added functionality to the earbuds that use the chip, like the AirPods Pro 3. These features include adaptive audio, conversation awareness, personalized volume, voice isolation, and live translation. [Image: [Image: Adaptive audio blends ANC and transparency to adjust to noise around you while still allowing you to be more aware, and is my preferred listening mode on Apple headphones and earbuds. I find Apple hits the ANC / transparency blend the best, and even though you can’t manually adjust the intensity like with Sony products, I don’t feel the need to. I also have friends that lean on live translation for interactions in their daily lives. Conversation awareness can be useful, although it doesn’t always react fast enough, and I prefer to take my headphones off when speaking to someone — for courtesy, at the very least. And voice isolation works well, but the clarity of my voice during phone calls wasn’t quite as good as I get with Sony headphones. Like other Apple headphones, if you connect the Max 2 to a non-Apple device you lose access to much of this functionality. Noise cancellation can still be toggled with the listening mode button, but auto switching, Siri gestures, fast pairing, spatial audio, and adaptive audio are not usable. Apart from the H2 chip and improved sound and ANC, the Max 2 are the same as the original — including the flaws. They’re solidly built, with a stainless steel headband and telescoping arms, aluminum ear cups, a knit mesh canopy headband, and memory foam ear cushions; they feel higher-end than the primarily plastic Sony and Bose headphones. But they’re also still really heavy at 385 grams — the Sony WH-1000XM6 and Bose Ultra Headphones both come in around 254 grams — and their clamping force can be too much for some. During my testing I was able to wear them for a couple hours before feeling the pressure on the top of my head and in front of my ears, but a friend had trouble wearing them for more than a half hour. Another issue that Apple decided not to fix, and which has been a common complaint since the original Max released, is the poor excuse for a case, which is really just a flexible wrap for the ear cups that puts the headphones into a deep sleep state. It offers virtually no protection for the headphones, especially the mesh headband. I could never see myself feeling comfortable putting the Max 2 in their case and tossing it in my bag or luggage without worry that something would damage or scratch them. Sony, Bose, Sennheiser, and B&W all include some form of structured case to protect their multi-hundred-dollar headphones. I would have expected Apple to release a separate (and expensive) hard case sometime in the past six years, but at this point I don’t think it will. [Image: [Image: There’s also still no way to truly turn them off. While I like the simplicity of the listening mode button and digital crown, I still wish there was a toggle to completely power them down. Is it a big deal? They enter into a deep sleep when put in their “case” and a fully charged battery will last months in that state, so it’s not a major exclusion. But for my own peace of mind I wish the option was available. And then there’s the price. Even with the increase to headphones pricing seen over the last year, at $549 Apple’s AirPods Max 2 are still around $100 more expensive than the Sony XM6 and Bose Ultra Headphones at their regular prices. There’s no doubt the AirPods Max 2 are great headphones. They sound incredible, support spatial audio (for those who enjoy it), and have top-of-the-line ANC. They’re also very easy and intuitive to use with other Apple products thanks to fast pair and iCloud device switching. If you own the first-gen Max — especially the Lightning version — the AirPods Max 2 will be a great, albeit expensive, upgrade. But I don’t think they’re the right headphones for the majority of people. Both the Sony XM6 and Bose Ultra are better options, especially outside of the Apple ecosystem, where the Max 2 lose many of their best features. They both sound good (although I’d say the Max 2 are a bit better than both) and have excellent noise cancellation, and they have better multipoint connection if you’re not all in on Apple. Plus, they’re less expensive, are lighter, and have better travel cases. It’s frustrating, because with a few design tweaks, and a case that actually works as a case, the Max 2 could have been the perfect Apple headphones I’ve wanted for years. Instead, I’ll have to wait for the AirPods Max 3. Photography by Amelia Holowaty Krales / The Verge

articles.title: Dealer's Choice Walkthrough: Cut or Pure? - GTA 6 Guide - IGN
articles.summary: Jason’s been instructed to run a drug deal by Boobie, and Dre’Quan insists on joining. Grand Theft Auto VI’s Chapter 3 mission,
articles.body:
Jason’s been instructed to run a drug deal by Boobie, and Dre’Quan insists on joining. Grand Theft Auto VI ’s Chapter 3 mission , Dealer’s Choice, has a number of variations depending on a few key choices, and this official IGN GTA 6 guide walks you through it.

Click on a link below to jump to that section of this guide:

Return to the Jack of Hearts to meet Dre’Quan. You can spend time in the strip club before heading up to him (you’ll want to have a few hundred in cash to make the most of the services if you’re interested), but when you’re ready to get the mission started, go upstairs to the studio. You’ll find Dre’Quan in the middle of a recording session.

If you don’t want to sit through the recording session, look at Dre’Quan and ask to Visit Boobie. If you interrupt the session, you’ll miss a choice to help Dre’Quan make a creative decision about the song they’re recording.

Follow Dre’Quan up to Boobie’s office to learn more about the mission. It seems Boobie needs help with his drug business. At the end of the scene, Jason and Dre’Quan leave the club together and walk toward Dre’Quan’s car, a Benefactor Dubsta. Drive to the marked pickup spot not far off to continue.

Follow Dre’Quan through the apartment complex and up the stairs to a corner apartment. Inside, the dealer, Tyrone, discusses an artist he wants to connect with Dre’Quan. You can interrupt Dre’Quan and Tyrone’s conversation by asking Tyrone about the “Stuff?” or you can wait for the conversation to conclude. If you interrupt, Tap to Reveal

Tyrone signals to his people to bring out the product. He gives you two choices: pure or cut. Boobie said if you take the cut product and sell it, you can potentially make a bit extra money.

Your choice between the two products determines how the deal goes. If you’ve got the genuine stuff, it’s more likely the deal will go smoothly. Convincing the buyers to take the cut product won’t be so simple.

After you’ve made your choice, follow Dre’Quan out of the apartment complex and back to his car. The deal location is incredibly close. Follow the GPS to a nearby neighborhood and park by the homes as instructed. Dre’Quan talks to Jason as they make a short walk to the deal.

Click the option you choose below for guidance on how to approach the next section. As always, there are other ways to approach the situation other than what’s detailed below.

If you chose to sell pure product, you’ve picked the smoothest deal option possible. When Dre’Quan asks, hand over the product to the men. One takes the bag into a car to inspect what you’re offering. You can stand around and wait for them to finish, or you can speed the mission along and ask the buyer for the money. Jason asks about the money one way or the other, progressing the deal.

Since you picked the pure product, you’ll have a straightforward transaction with the buyers – even if they took a while to get it sorted. Take the money from the car and leave with Dre’Quan.

As you approach Dre’Quan’s Dubsta, a man steps out from behind the dumpster and begins harassing Jason. If you’re looking to keep the deal clean, tell the man to ask someone else. Then, when he approaches with the wrench, punch the guy out rather than giving him the bag or pulling your gun. Shooting him could attract the attention of cops, but how you want to proceed with the encounter is up to you.

Get in the driver’s side of Dre’Quan’s car and drive off to begin the debrief of the mission. He’ll ask you to drive him to another spot, but as you drive and they talk, the scene fades to black and into the ending cutscene.

The deal begins in earnest after you hand over the bag. The man inspecting the product quickly realizes it’s tainted, prompting the guards and buyer to pull their weapons. How you proceed next changes the rest of the mission significantly, including how much you’ll make off the product. If you focus on the buyer, you can attempt to defuse the situation.

My Bad, Half Price? ($) – You’ll successfully defuse the situation, but you’ll lose out on profits.

Take It or Leave It ($$$$) – If you don’t make your choice in time, this is the default option. Selecting this leads to a shootout.

Jason offers the drugs at two for the price of one. The buyers accept the deal and give you the money in the backpack, allowing Dre’Quan and Jason to leave the neighborhood peacefully as they talk.

Get in the driver’s side of Dre’Quan’s car and drive off to begin the debrief of the mission. He’ll ask you to drive him to another location, but as you drive and they talk, the scene fades to black and into the ending cutscene.

You chose aggression, and the buyer and his guards are ready to match it. You’ll have a few short seconds to press Square / X before Jason is shot in the head. Reacting on time allows you to knock out the guy while Dre’Quan reacts too. Move quickly to knock out or shoot anyone left standing. The faster you start shooting, though, the faster you’ll get a response from the buyer’s allies around the neighborhood.

No matter how you choose to proceed, you must grab the bag of money from the back of the car if you want to get paid. There’s a FRA Assault Rifle on the trunk that’ll be useful for the retreat back to the car, too. As you grab the goods, folks from the homes and street start shooting at you and Dre’Quan. All you need to do now is get back to Dre’s car and escape. You’ll encounter a number of enemies and their reinforcements who are shooting to kill, so be careful and try to stay low. Adrenaline is helpful here if you have any.

So long as you got the money, you’ll get your payment for the job later. The mission ends as Jason drives off with Dre, or if you ditched him, you’ll escape alone.

The mission’s final cutscene shifts to the next morning with a surprise visitor at the apartment. Jason, Lucia, and their guest talk about what’s next for them and the mysterious hard drive.

With the mission over, you can swap freely between Jason and Lucia again, and there’s plenty to do! If you want to stick with main and optional missions, you’ll have these available, plus any others you’ve yet to complete that you picked up in previous chapters:

Speak with Tyrone – Jason Only This is added to the to-do list of story missions a short time after you’ve completed Dealer’s Choice. Boobie texts Jason.

This is added to the to-do list of story missions a short time after you’ve completed Dealer’s Choice. Boobie texts Jason.

Talk to Boobie – Jason Only Dre’Quan calls Jason a short time after completing Dealer’s Choice, saying Boobie wants Jason to be his driver.

Dre’Quan calls Jason a short time after completing Dealer’s Choice, saying Boobie wants Jason to be his driver.

Join a Street Race – Hit ‘n’ Run VC – If you’re looking to do some street races, join a street race in Salton to earn some cash and make new contacts.

Save for the Future – This optional mission is ongoing and serves as a tracker for how much you’ve invested in the Family Savings account.

You’ll have to wait for information on the encrypted hard drive. At this point, though, you’ll start getting more activities and missions that can be completed with only one character or specifically require Jason or Lucia. Press D-pad Right to open the character overlay, and there, you can choose to invite your partner out or ask to split up if they’re already with you. You can also text or call them to ask them to meet up. There’s plenty to explore in Vice City and beyond.

While driving on a freeway in GTA 6, you might randomly stumble upon a traffic jam caused by an animal rights activist group called the Dodos Rising . This group has made it their mission to liberate animals from zoos, cages, and aquariums, as well as stop fracking. This official GTA 6 guide provides a full quest walkthrough for the Dodos Rising Optional Mission , including how to start Dodos Rising, and the recommended order in which you should complete the missions.

Need help completing any of the four missions in this questline? Click the links below to jump to:

How to Start Dodos Rising Mission: Dodo Freeway Protest

While driving on a freeway, you may come across one of these Dodo protest groups. They will be blocking traffic and harassing a Leonida Animal Service vehicle.

As you approach, there will be two members of the Dodos Rising group at the back of the truck trying to break it open. You can target one of them after they ask for help and agree to help them. Using Focus Mode, you’ll see that there is a lock on the left handle of the truck. Shoot the lock with a pistol, which will cause all the Dodos to cheer.

One of the members of the Dodos will open the back of the truck and climb in to rescue a polar bear. This doesn’t go so well. Once the polar bear’s cage is open, it will attack and kill the man instantly.

The polar bear will then jump out of the back of the truck and kill another member of the group. After that, the polar bear will run away, and all the protesters will flee. You aren’t given any clue what to do after this, and this isn’t even needed to start the Dodos Rising optional mission. Feel free to leave the area.

To start the Dodos Rising optional mission, you’ll need to visit an aquarium in Catalan Key, or a Monkey Lab in south VCIA. You can do the aquarium or the monkey lab in any order. For this guide, we will be doing the Dodos Rising optional mission in this order:

After completing those missions, the overall mission will converge at the fracking mission, Twin Flames , leading into the finale, Dodo, Rise! .

After the Dodo, Rise! mission ends, you will eventually receive a text message directly from Yvonne letting you know that the Dodos will likely not contact you anymore, but that they have some money for you. articles.title: Robbing Banks is a Blast, But I Wish There Were More Houses to Repair in GTA 6
articles.summary: Forget sticking things up with a shotgun, I want to fix things up with a nailgun.
articles.body:
My first weekend with Grand Theft Auto 6 was truly mindblowing. The first 20 or so hours I’ve spent with Rockstar’s triumphant return to Vice City have transported me to an impossibly high fidelity game world and treated me to criminal capers so immaculately crafted they make Michael Mann seem more like a Michael mouse. As I’ve made my way across the sprawling Leonida map I’ve relished each and every unethical exploit of lawbreaking lovebirds, Jason and Lucia. So far I’ve been Jason the wheelman, Jason the bagman, and Jason the hitman, but to my surprise, what I really want to be is… Tim the Toolman?

Before you hit me with one of Tim Allen’s trademark quizzical caveman grunts, let me back up for a moment. In case you’re not one of the more than 20 million players who gleefully jumped into Rockstar’s latest crime epic on day one, GTA 6’s opening hours present a number of optional tasks that you can undertake as Jason in an effort to make his girlfriend Lucia’s arrival at your love nest a little more loved-up. You can visit the grocery store to line the kitchen pantry with protein bars and packets of chips, pick up a bouquet of flowers, and even splash out on a customised necklace from a local jeweler if you really want to boost your relationship status to Boyfriend of the Year levels.

I ticked off these tasks more out of open-world obligation than any particularly earnest desire to impress my virtual girlfriend; they were pink dots on my minimap, so my well-trained gamer instincts compelled me to clear them. But what I did derive a surprising amount of satisfaction from, was running down the shortlist of repairs to Jason’s dilapidated waterfront home. Drilling in drywall panels in the bedroom and applying a warm shade of peach-coloured paint to them with a roller. Climbing a ladder onto the roof and fastening fresh shingles to it with a nailgun to stop the ceiling leaks. Replacing the rotten steps leading to the front door with some fresh planks of wood. Each of these tasks provided me with moments of zen far more relaxing than the game's own dedicated meditation minigame. I even took a moment to stop and marvel at the impeccably well-rendered tools in Jason’s shed.

I enjoyed fussing around on Jason’s fixer-upper so much that I must admit I was a little deflated to discover that once this brief burst of renovations are complete, that seems to be it as far as the cosy home makeover minigames are concerned. A lot of the other features of GTA 6 are presented as an appetite-whetting taster before they become ongoing activities to pursue at your leisure for the rest of the story; you go on a short hunting trip with one of Jason’s old army buddies, and from then on you’re free to stalk deer and bears in the Leonida wilderness. You complete a dirt-encrusted drive in an opening event at the Thrillbilly Mud Club, and afterwards you’re free to indulge in spectacular stunt jumps, hill climbs, and a variety of races on the MotorStorm-style circuits.

Completing Jason’s home repairs, however, doesn’t seem to unlock any form of handyman activities to pursue around the map. I envisaged clearing out the longarms and bulletproof vests stashed in the bed of Jason’s truck and loading it up with power tools and paint cans to go do some odd jobs around the neighbourhood – or perhaps even buying run-down properties, fixing them up, and then flipping them to quickly boost Jason and Lucia’s shared bank account. But after speaking with other members of IGN who’ve rolled credits in GTA 6, it doesn’t sound like Jason ever gets another opportunity to pick up his tools again, other than to grab a hammer or shovel to smack hillbillies around with when he’s in the process of stealing the profits from their meth lab.

Now, I know what you’re thinking reading this; if he wanted to do home restorations in a video game, there’s no shortage of quality options out there that could scratch that itch, from The Sims 4 to House Flipper to Powerwash Simulator. I also know what you’re thinking if you happen to be my wife reading this; there’s no shortage of DIY projects I could be spending my Saturday doing around my actual house instead of sitting on the couch complaining of the lack of virtual repair jobs to complete in a video game. (I’ll get to them next weekend, I promise.)

However, I think a big part of the reason that I’d like to do more repairwork in GTA 6 is because this is undoubtedly the most beautiful and believable game world I’ve ever inhabited, and thus I feel an innate urge to preserve it. In fact, unlike any GTA game before it, I’ve found myself really focussing on how much life there is in the environment as opposed to creating my typical trails of death, strapping on a scuba tank and playing with porpoises in the depths of the Atlantic Ocean, or peering at pelicans through the in-game binoculars. I’m only a couple of chapters into the story, but so far I wholeheartedly agree with Luke Reilly’s 10 out of 10 review . GTA 6 is clearly a masterpiece, and one that doesn’t really leave much room for improvement. But, even so, I can’t help but wish it had a few more rooms for improvement.

These are the things I’m thinking about as I drive around Vice City and its surroundings. While most players are probably scanning strip malls for potential stores to rob, I’m eyeballing side streets for run-down homes in need of a fresh coat of paint or a replacement screen door. Sure, I’m still having an amazing time stealing unique cars and searching for moonlit monsters with a flashlight in flooded swampland areas but, even as I indulge in each incredible new gameplay surprise and jaw-dropping action set piece that GTA 6 serves up, a part of me still wishes I could take an occasional break to paint fences and sand decks like I’m subtly being taught the basics of karate by an aging Japanese gentleman from Okinawa.

Of course, given that this is a GTA game there could be plenty of nefarious ways to incorporate the handyman gameplay too. Perhaps you could don a disguise and smash up a storefront, leave and change your clothes, and then come back and offer your services to replace the glass window panels for cash in hand. Or maybe you could operate like The Wolf in Pulp Fiction, receiving urgent calls from other criminals to come and clean up their messes, potentially even using the same powerwashing mechanic you employ on Brian’s boat early in the game to hose the brains out of their backseat.

I don’t want to make it seem like I’m not seeing the floodplains for the cypress trees here; GTA 6 has a dizzying to-do list and an unprecedented ability to provide delightful distractions at every turn. Each time I boot it up I find something new that surprises or excites me, whether it’s a banger I’ve not yet heard on the in-game radio or a bizarre encounter with a local bovine with a burgeoning social media presence . I also understand that the team at Rockstar North had to make some sacrifices in terms of the time and cost to finally get this ambitious behemoth out the door and into gamers’ hands . It’s possible the developers wanted to give players more houses to remodel but, like darts and bowling, they just didn’t make the cut.

But I do hold out hope that the home improvement activity could resurface in a future update, or perhaps once GTA Online eventually arrives in Leonida. Because although I’m having a ridiculously good time attempting to build a criminal empire, I still wish I could slow down to build a few patios along the way. Am I the only one?

Tristan Ogilvie is a senior video editor at IGN based in Sydney, Australia. He has 25 years of experience covering video games, having served as Deputy Editor on Official PlayStation 2 Magazine Australia and as Editor of Official Xbox 360 Magazine Australia, before joining IGN in 2009. articles.title: Naughty Dog Dev: GTA 6 Appears to Him ‘as a Bugatti Veyron Would to a Nervous Victorian Child’
articles.summary: Developers are stunned at how dramatically advanced GTA 6 is.
articles.body:
Just like the rest of us, developers the world over are playing GTA 6. Just like the rest of us, they’re also finding themselves blown away by just how dramatically advanced and impressive GTA 6 is proving to be. However, as professionals with a far, far firmer idea of how the sausage gets made than regular punters, precisely how impressed some developers are is speaking volumes about just what a technical achievement GTA 6 really does represent.

Naughty Dog world design director Michael Barclay, presently working on Intergalactic: The Heretic Prophet, minces no words.

“I’ve made video games for 19 years and GTA VI appears to me as a Bugatti Veyron would to a nervous Victorian child,” writes Barclay via social media.

Barclay is far from alone, with a host of developers in the replies to Barclay’s comment expressing like sentiments in the days following GTA 6’s release.

Payday 2 game director David Goldfarb, who previously worked on Mirror’s Edge and a variety of Battlefield games, is similarly stunned.

“Been making games over 30 years… Can’t even find words for what I’m playing now,” he writes , later noting he’s “never been this floored by anything ever.”

Character artist Del Walker (Suicide Squad: Kill the Justice League, The Last of Us: Part II, Star Wars: Jedi - Survivor) quips he simply can’t explain what he’s seeing despite his background in the business.

“Every GTA clip gets sent to me in the group chat with. ‘You’re a game dev. How did they do this?” he writes. “Brother, I wasn’t there when they opened the portal? This is not magic I recognize.”

GTA 6 arrived late last week, smashing records as the biggest entertainment launch of all time, with retail sales reaching $3.79 billion in its first 24 hours. In my review for IGN I called it “the single most impressive video game I have ever played,” something that is making increasingly more sense to me the more other developers I note making comments like the above.

Just getting started in GTA 6, or wondering what to do next? You can get stuck into the Official Grand Theft Auto 6 guide right here on IGN, consult our Beginner's Guide or Leonida interactive map , or get an idea of all the incredible flourishes to keep an eye out for by checking out our look at 99 incredible details you can find in GTA 6.

articles.title: Avengers: Doomsday Runtime Revealed as Trailer Teased for Today
articles.summary: Fans are expecting a fresh Avengers: Doomsday trailer today, and now have a good idea of the movie's runtime.
articles.body:
Fans are expecting a fresh Avengers: Doomsday trailer today, and now have a good idea of the movie's runtime.

With Marvel's highly-anticipated blockbuster less than a month away, viewers are awaiting a chunky new look at the film after what feels like a long wait. Happily, however, that wait seems to be at its end — according to Peggy Carter actress Hayley Atwell.

"There's a new trailer dropping on Monday... am I allowed to have said that?" Atwell told fans in New York over the weekend while signing autographs, according to Deadline . (We're guessing that no, she probably wasn't allowed to say that.)

Avengers: Doomsday Poster Montage Gallery

If Atwell's intel is correct, this would be our first substantial look at Doomsday in months. Marvel began its rollout of Doomsday teasers last December, when it started launching a series of teasers focused on Steve Rogers, Thor, the X-Men and then the Wakandans plus Fantastic Four. A proper trailer then followed in July, showing our first look at Robert Downey Jr. in character as Doctor Doom. Now, with the movie imminent, fans want more.

Over the past year, Marvel has dropped a few more hints and tidbits, and in the past few weeks fans have got confirmation that Elizabeth Olsen is back in the MCU as her fan-favorite character Scarlet Witch, while Kate Bishop actress Hailee Steinfeld has just confirmed her own Doomsday return . (Fans also strongly suspect Ms. Marvel actress Iman Vellani is on the cusp of her own Doomsday confirmation, since she appears to be sitting on the same kind of Doomsday set chair for recent episodes of her official Marvel podcast.)

This year's other MCU releases also featured fresh story beats that connected with Doomsday, with the end of Spider-Man: Brand New Day teasing a Spidey in space, while Avengers: Endgame Encore included looks at what Steve Rogers, the Hulk, and the TVA where up to as Doctor Doom arrives.

The Most Surprising Avengers and Marvel Characters Not Announced for Doomsday

"We’ve done a series of tags around the characters because the story actually started [with the Steve Rogers teaser]," Doomsday co-director Joe Russo said during a chat with the Qatar Film Committee. "And you’ve been watching it slowly unfold and these are all pieces of something that are going to equal two and a half hours of your time on December 18," he continued, apparently confirming the movie will run to around 150 minutes.

This would make the film the same length as 2018's similar Avengers movie Infinity War, and shorter than Eternals, Black Panther: Wakanda Forever, and the three-hour Avengers: Endgame.

Here's hoping Atwell is correct and we're just hours away from seeing more of what those 150 minutes will contain. Either way, Avengers: Doomsday launches on December 18.

articles.title: The Last Jedi Director Rian Johnson Finally Addresses Whether He'd Ever Return to Star Wars
articles.summary: Star Wars: The Last Jedi director Rian Johnson has revealed whether he'd ever return to the galaxy far, far away.
articles.body:
Star Wars: The Last Jedi director Rian Johnson has revealed whether he'd ever return to the galaxy far, far away.

Speaking this weekend at the Marrakech Film Festival, Johnson was asked for his thoughts on eventually returning to the Star Wars universe, almost a decade on from his divisive sequel trilogy entry. Perhaps surprisingly, Johnson suggested he was still open to the idea — despite the intense backlash to his movie from some of Star Wars' noisest followers.

"I mean, I love Star Wars more now than I ever have," Johnson began (thanks, Variety ). "And it's exciting to me that there are a lot of different voices now, taking cracks at it.

Rian Johnson Movies and Shows to Watch After The Last Jedi

"In terms of... I'm already writing the next thing I’m gonna do, and it's not a Star Wars thing or a Knives Out thing," Johnson revealed. "Right now, I'm very much enjoying making my own stuff, but if the opportunity presented itself, it's a world I deeply love.

"It's also a group of people I deeply love," he concluded. "[Lucasfilm's new co-president] Dave Filoni I got to know making The Last Jedi, I think he's a wonderful, wonderful guy who really has the spirit of Star Wars in him. All the Lucasfilm folks are awesome."

When The Last Jedi launched in 2017 as the second film in Disney's Star Wars sequel trilogy, it received positive critical reviews before a surge of fan criticism took hold. Johnson later said that he anticipated some of this response, and was proud of having made a film that took some bold narrative steps and did more than simply feed fans what they'd expected. Lucasfilm seemed less proud, however, and ensured that elements of The Last Jedi's story were retconned for its bland trilogy closer Rise of Skywalker, while discussions for a whole new trilogy of films led by Johnson fell off the radar completely.

In the meantime, Johnson has finally found widespread success with his Knives Out movie trilogy, for which he has served as writer, director and co-producer. Former Bond star Daniel Craig has led a starry cast in three murder mystery whodunnits so far, released between 2019 and 2025, with a fourth entry expected down the line.

As for Star Wars, while Johnson appears to be leaving the door open to his return some day, Lucasfilm doesn't appear interested at present. Beyond the upcoming Star Wars: Starfighter, which lands in theaters on May 28, the Star Wars production company is yet to lay out a long term vision for the franchise following its recent leadership changes, various short-lived Disney+ TV projects, and a lengthy slate of movie projects cancelled or stuck in development hell. Not even a big screen outing for The Mandalorian and Grogu this year could turn things around, as the movie set a disappointing record for the franchise's lowest live-action theatrical gross.

Fans expect that Filoni and Lucasfilm will use Star Wars' upcoming 50th anniversary year to map out what's next for the franchise in broader detail over the coming 12 moths. Reports suggest that of everything Lucasfilm has previously announced, the new movie/trilogy written by Dark Phoenix's Simon Kinberg is the one currently moving forward . Whether Filoni will also be involved again with Star Wars anytime soon, however, remains to be seen.

articles.title: 'The System Is Not Good Vs. Evil': Why GTA 6's Criminal Profile Mechanic Is Dividing Fans
articles.summary: GTA 6 players are debating the game's Criminal Profile system, and how it operates with more depth than just a straightforward "good vs. evil" morality system.
articles.body:
GTA 6 players are debating the game's Criminal Profile scale, and how it operates with more depth than just a straightforward "good vs. evil" morality system.

While previous Rockstar adventures have operated on a simpler, binary scale, GTA 6 offers a more nuanced Criminal Profile that reflects your playstyle — from silent and stealthy to excessively violent and "psycho." But some players have criticised how the gameplay mechanic appears to penalise actions taken in self-defence, while others have suggested it is just not well explained.

From "Professional" all the way to "Irredeemable," GTA 6 tracks each character's actions across a series of five profile labels — and yes, you can make Jason and Lucia have wildly different personalities from each other, depending on your actions as either. But Professional does not mean pacifist, and players will inevitably still rack up a fair body count as they explore more of Leonida — the difference here is how messy you are along the way.

The scale begins with Professional, which reflects actions that align with an undetected or non-lethal play style. Stealth takedowns and non-lethal incapacitations award a focus boost, as do kind acts towards NPCs. Go for limbs (highlighted in yellow while in bullet time) rather than headshots to keep this rating intact, or earn points back towards it if you're currently rated as more wantonly violent.

Next up is Hardened, which reflects a slightly less cautious approach to firefights and taking lives in general. You're headshotting the bad guys rather than incapacitating them, in other words, but not mowing down the innocent cops who try and stop you on the way out.

Turn things up a notch and you get to Violent, where cops and random passers by are being caught up in your rampage. It's at this level that your focus boost switches to pulling off headshots, reflecting your own more violent playstyle. But there's still a way to go yet before you're playing GTA 6 at your worst.

Slip into Pyscho rank and you'll have left a lot of defenceless people and animals smeared across the tarmac or piled up in artfully arranged piles of corpses. It's a this rank that cops are so tired of your bulls**t that the option to surrender gets removed, and probably fair enough.

And then there's Irredeemable. If you don't revert from Psycho after a while — and ignore multiple in-game warnings — you'll permanently slip into Irredeemable territory for the rest of your playthrough. There no way to change your Criminal Profile again and you'll also lose the ability to boost focus, making combat harder. Additionally, there are also story implications — which we won't spoil here.

What seems to be confusing some players is the idea that some killing is accepted by the game even at the game's lowest Criminal Profile ranks, though this appears to be contextual. Headshot a gang member in a hideout after shooting most enemies in the knees and you're unlikely to be seen as too naughty. But fight back against an NPC on the street, or fire at a bank teller rather than simply intimidating them, and the game will take notice.

"The idea of violent vs. professional criminal sounded awesome on paper, but the fact it punishes you for literal SELF-DEFENSE just because you go for headshots is ridiculous to me," wrote content creator Synth Potato in a widely-shared post on X/Twitter. "Carjacking being considered a bad action is also just not thought out enough. By definition it is not a violent crime if no one got hurt, so carjacking is not one. Red Dead 2 did this way better, it made way more sense what is an evil action and what isn't."

"It's important to realize the system is not 'good vs evil' but 'professional criminal vs psychopath,'" countered one reply from GTA fan The24thFrame . "A professional already has their getaway car prepared. A psycho runs into traffic and forces someone out of their car. In my experience you don't have to be *too* stressed about it," they continued. "I have been maintaining 'professional' without issue and I still probably kill about 25% of the enemies. Especially in the more action-heavy missions."

"This," agreed another fan, the appropriately named SirSnipeyy . "I'm profesional BECAUSE I park my car around the corner so it's not seen, I shoot limbs on sight if they pull guns or punch them, I pick locks, wipe tapes, turn off alarms, have outfits ready in the trunk, and escape route planned, and a body shop nearby if needed. It's cool."

"It's a 'Michael to Trevor' scale tbh," wrote wildstar33 , summing up the Character Profile mechanic in a nutshell.

Still, others have said this is not how they played GTA in the past, and prefer the series' previous ability to cause widespread mayhem without consequence. Of course, you can still do that if that's how you want to play the game — but in a story that attempts some level of realism in its character relationships and overall narrative arc, Character Profiles seemingly feel like an attempt at keeping the game grounded.

articles.title: GTA 6 Motion Capture Actor Has No Idea Who He Is in the Game, Sparks Social Media Hunt to Find His Character
articles.summary: One GTA 6 actor has no idea who he plays and has asked for fans to help him find his character in the game.
articles.body:
One GTA 6 actor has no idea who he plays and has asked for fans to help him find his character in the game. Guy A. Fortt, who has previously played a guard in Jessica Jones and The Sopranos, did some performance capture work on GTA 6, but the secrecy of the project meant he didn’t have much context for his scenes.

Actors are often kept in the dark when playing a part in Rockstar games. When Roger Clark auditioned for Red Dead Redemption 2 , for example, the only clue he had at the time was he was told to wear cowboy boots. That secrecy, combined with the time between performance and the game’s release, hasn’t helped in Fortt’s case.

“So, I was a motion capture actor on GTA 6, but I don’t know who the hell I am,” Fortt explained in a video that went viral on Instagram . “I auditioned about four or five years ago, they put the balls all over my body and face … and then I forgot all about it.”

“Then I get a random email telling me that I’m in GTA 6. This is where I need your help.”

Fortt, who is 63 years old and doesn't have a PS5 or play video games himself, is looking for help tracking the character down. According to the actor, his performance saw him standing behind a counter of some kind, and he interacted with Jason and Lucia at one point.

He could be some kind of store clerk, a receptionist, or even a cop at a desk, judging by his description. It would be very funny if he ended up being a guard again, like in Jessica Jones and The Sopranos.

The community is currently on the hunt for his character, but it might take a while. Rockstar put lots of work into making GTA 6 NPCs varied , hiring dozens and dozens of actors to breathe life into the citizens of Leonida. In a follow-up social media post on day two of the hunt, Fortt said 3 million people were looking for his character in the game, but no luck yet. I assume that's based on social media impressions to his various posts on this, rather than people actively looking for his character in the game. But still, he's caught quite a bit of attention for this.

articles.title: Blade Runner 2099, the Disappointing Continuation of the Iconic Franchise, Reminds Us That It's Quite an Experience to Live in Fear, Isn't It?
articles.summary: Review: Blade Runner 2099 is a disappointing continuation of the iconic series with miscast leads and a propensity to fan service.
articles.body:
All eight episodes of Blade Runner 2099 debut on Prime Video on November 25. This is a spoiler-free review.

There’s a scene in 2017’s Blade Runner 2049 where the very grim and serious Agent K (Ryan Gosling) makes a joke about a Wallace Corp. employee’s lost baby pictures. “Well, it’s a shame… you must’ve been adorable,” K says straight-faced. It’s a moment of levity in a pretty heavy movie, with Gosling playing it without even cracking a smile, and it works wonderfully to keep us afloat amid all the darkness – as do several other such instances in the film.

The people behind Blade Runner 2099, the latest installment in the series which began with the 1982 Ridley Scott/Harrison Ford movie , don’t understand this, or at the very least don’t think they need to include such moments of humor or lightness in their new show. As a result, watching Blade Runner 2099 very quickly turns into a slog, leading to an increasing feeling with each passing episode that the show is crushing inward on you like the teeming, downtrodden masses of its futuristic Los Angeles.

It’s not just the oh-so-serious scripting that leads to this unforced error, however. 2099 also suffers from the performances of leads Michelle Yeoh and Hunter Schafer, who seem to be trying to out-gloom each other for most of these eight episodes. The result is a buddy-cop story where the cops not only aren’t buddies, but are also unappealing and ultimately a drag to be around. Where’s Harrison Ford and his noodles when you need them!?

Set 50 years after 2049 (obviously), and 80 years after Ford’s Deckard was Blading and Running, the new series picks up the threads of the Replicant revolution that was just about to get underway in that previous film. In the intervening decades, the Replicants – humanoid robots formerly used as slave labor, for those who have never actually seen a Blade Runner movie (and judging by box office figures, there are a lot of you) – won that war. So now, that which man made rules over man. And they’re not terribly nice about it, either!

Yeoh – who after the Star Trek disaster that was Section 31 two years ago and now this misfire may want to reconsider the whole small screen sci-fi thing – stars as Olwen, a Replicant Blade Runner whose built-in termination date is nearing. She’s seen things you people wouldn’t believe, don’t you know, having lived Off-World in the past – something the franchise has only spoken about in previous iterations but never shown until now – but now she’s ready to head off to the great unknown like all Replicants must do…

Enter Schafer as Cora, a human who through a confluence of events winds up having to pretend to be a Replicant, and not just a Replicant, but a Replicant Blade Runner working among other Replicant Blade Runners. And those Replicant Blade Runners are smart! And wily! And dangerous! And as I said earlier, not terribly nice. It’s a tricky situation for Cora, and the constant look of paralyzed terror on her face is completely credible and understandable, given her situation. The only problem is that look becomes Schafer’s main mode for 2099, and when combined with Olwen’s icy shoot-first, put-a-weird-bag-over-your-head-that-shoves-a-tube-down-your-throat-later philosophy, the viewer may very quickly find themselves wondering who they’re rooting for here, or why.

Indeed, as the story progresses, involving the hunt for some mysterious information from deep in the Blade Runner past, there are a few supporting characters who are given a short time in the spotlight and actually prove that 2099 has inhabitants that are, you know, interesting. For example, this far into the future the Voight-Kampff machine – the device used to probe Replicants for empathy, or a lack thereof – has been replaced by human children who are seemingly sold by their parents into a life of indentured servitude and trained to be living empathy detectors. Katelyn Rose Downey plays one such child, a scary, inscrutable creature when we first meet her… until we get a bit of an origin story for her in a later episode. Then there’s Matthew Needham (Larys on House of the Dragon), who plays another Replicant who is smart, scary, and entirely dismissive of humanity. “Your whole world has already gone past you,” he says of mankind. Amy Lennox also appears as a Replicant, sort of cut from the Pris mode from the original film in that she’s child-like yet deadly. But most importantly, whenever she’s onscreen, it’s a reprieve from the constipated angst of our two leads.

And look, as a lifetime Blade Runner devotee – I saw the original film when it was first released in a drive-in with my parents! – I take no pleasure in dismissing 2099. I’m also fully aware that the whole thing about Blade Runner is being dark and dreary, with Ford’s Deckard complaining about his ex-wife (depending on which cut you watched) and Gosling’s K on a doomed mission of self-salvation and so on. Those guys weren’t exactly a barrel of laughs, but they did have a charisma that let their characters be part of the Blade Runner dystopia without being engulfed by it. That’s not the case here.

Which isn’t to say that 2099 doesn’t have its merits. Certainly the production is a wonder to behold – how they make these shows that look like big-budget movies these days and don’t break the bank is beyond me. This is the Los Angeles (and elsewhere) of Blade Runner, without a doubt, and every flying spinner car and Tyrell Corporation tower is perfectly realized. The costuming is, well, interesting at times, seemingly competing for the biggest shoulder pads in the history of shoulder pads, but hey, it’s the future!

And creator Silka Luisa (Shining Girls) and her staff make it clear that they understand the source material that they’re building on, not just in terms of the films but also the Philip K. Dick book on which it’s all based, Do Androids Dream of Electric Sheep? The trailers have already hinted at the inclusion of the book’s TV host Buster Friendly, but there are other aspects of the book that the show has time to touch upon which fans will appreciate. The fandom among the creative team is strong, but at times 2099 tries too hard to evoke the feel of the previous films, the 1982 original in particular. Ever wanted to see Rachael’s implanted memory of the spider outside her window? Well, you may be in luck here… or not, as the case may be.

articles.title: Nvidia Board Reinstates Jensen Huang as CEO Amid Donald Trump Social Media Pressure
articles.summary: The Nvidia board has reinstated Jensen Huang as President, CEO and Board Director amid social media pressure from Donald Trump.
articles.body:
The Nvidia board has reinstated Jensen Huang as President, CEO and Board Director amid social media pressure from Donald Trump.

Huang — who stepped down as Nvidia CEO amid a scandal involving infidelity and alleged espionage — rejoins the company after its Board of Directors “voted unanimously to reinstate Mr. Huang following a series of discussions and meetings with Mr. Huang, after which the Board was satisfied with respect to Mr. Huang’s candor and ability to lead Nvidia."

Huang resigned as Nvidia CEO on November 12 after reports of an affair with a woman U.S. officials suspect of working for Chinese intelligence. The suspicion has not been proven, and Huang has not been accused of criminal wrongdoing.

"In the process of reaching its decision, the Board received input from senior levels of the United States government, and based on that input, the Board is confident that Mr. Huang’s reinstatement poses no national security risk," Nvidia continued.

Last week, Huang said he was ready to return to the company he co-founded , while apologizing for the problems he'd caused both Nvidia and his family. In a statement issued at the time, Huang insisted he would be willing to return as CEO if Nvidia's Board of Directors decided it was in the best interest in the company. Some Nvidia employees and other tech CEOs had rallied to Huang's defense and called for him to be reinstated as CEO.

Nvidia's dramatic decision comes just hours after President Donald Trump called for Huang's reinstatement in a post on Truth Social. Trump said Huang's return would be best for both the company and the United States.

Harvey C. Jones, Chair of the Board, issued the following statement:

Jensen Huang issued a statement of his own:

Nvidia said today that it had formed a committee to investigate reports that Huang had been the target of a " foreign intelligence effort," and insisted the investigation will proceed. "Mr. Huang fully supports the investigation and is committed to cooperating with it," Nvidia said.

Nvidia and Huang still face tough questions about who was in charge of compliance at the company, as well as answers to reports of chip sales to China. Meanwhile, Nvidia said it had formed a National Security and Export Control Committee to oversee trade compliance and national security risks. Nvidia is on the hunt for a Chief Compliance Officer to oversee compliance across Nvidia and report to the Nominating and Corporate Governance Committee. "Nvidia will continue to cooperate with ongoing government investigations and inquiries," it said.

Huang is reportedly due to appear before the House Foreign Affairs, Intelligence and China Select Committees on December 1. "The American people need answers on Mr. Huang and Nvidia’s role in allowing dangerous PRC actors to access our most advanced chips, as well as the role of a potential Chinese intelligence asset in this scandal,” Reps. Brian Mast, R-Fla., John Moolenaar, R-Mich., and Rick Crawford, R-Ark., the chairs of the Foreign Affairs, China Select and Intelligence Committees, said in a statement reported by CNBC .

articles.title: Ariana Grande Holds Her Own Against Ben Stiller and Robert De Niro in Focker-In-Law, the New Meet the Parents Sequel
articles.summary: Ariana Grande holds her comedic own with Ben Stiller and Robert De Niro in Focker-In-Law, an amiable enough entry in this over-the-hill cringe comedy franchise.
articles.body:
Focker-In-Law is in theaters on November 25.

After 26 years and three films, Ben Stiller and Robert De Niro are back with another strained but silly installment in the Meet the Parents franchise. Focker-In-Law essentially retreads the premise of the 2000 film but this time with Stiller’s Greg Focker as the reluctant would-be father-in-law. It’s entirely predictable and formulaic but the players and the circumstances are just amiable enough to make it passably fun.

Greg (Stiller), his wife Pam (Teri Polo), and their adult twins Samantha (Beanie Feldstein) and Henry (Skyler Gisondo) converge on patriarch Jack Byrnes’ (De Niro) home to celebrate his 80th birthday. Samantha brings along her awkward but lovable boyfriend Eduardo (Eduardo Franco), while aspiring med student Henry introduces his folks to Olivia (Ariana Grande), the young woman he plans to pop the question to over the weekend. But in true Focker fashion, Greg has already soured things before he learns that the woman he had a bad encounter with on his flight was Henry’s girlfriend Olivia.

The weekend that follows sees Greg convinced that Olivia is, despite meeting with everyone else’s approval, up to no good. Greg repeatedly attempts to expose Olivia – a savvy former FBI hostage negotiator turned executive coach – which sees the two engage in a battle of wits the likes of which Greg has not faced since he first locked horns with Jack all those years ago.

As with the 2000 film, the combative premise pushes Greg into increasingly absurd and extreme antics while Olivia proves she’s sharp enough to remain neck-and-neck if not a step ahead of him throughout. Olivia isn’t related to Jack but she’s definitely his kindred spirit and game recognizes game. Played with a hefty dose of pluck by Grande, Olivia commands respect from men who otherwise underestimate her because of her looks or her small stature.

Grande acquits herself well here but the standout of the franchise’s new cast members is Skyler Gisondo as Henry, who lacks the nerve to establish boundaries with his infantilizing dad. The question of whether Olivia is manipulating Henry or has his best interests at heart is central to Greg’s single-minded mission to delay if not derail their engagement. Gisondo captures both the exasperation of having the likes of the well-meaning but perpetually ill-suited Greg Focker for a dad while never losing sight of the genuine affection he has for him.

Unfortunately, Beanie Feldstein isn’t really given much good material here as Samantha, who Greg has so coddled that she’s incapable of doing anything for herself. Her storyline is instead in service of her boyfriend Eduardo’s ambition to win a place in Jack’s Circle of Trust. Teri Polo is fairly marginalized with not much to accomplish in the story, while Blythe Danner barely registers as present as the Byrnes matriarch Dina. Faring a bit better is Owen Wilson, who reprises his recurring role as Pam’s wealthy ex, Kevin Rawley, who remains a beloved member of the Byrnes family much to Greg’s ongoing discomfort.

Turning 80, De Niro’s Jack has mellowed with age and is no longer as combative with Greg as he once was. Jack’s now on a health kick, which only gives vegan Olivia one more competitive advantage over Greg. De Niro seems to be having fun even if his delivery is mostly rote.

But this is Stiller’s movie and he continues to wring as much awkwardness as he can out of every rough situation of uncomfortable exchange Greg becomes ensnared in. So much of the humor and conflict in this movie is caused by Greg’s inability to ‘fess up to making a social faux pas and instead just digging the hole deeper for himself. The whole movie would be over in 10 minutes if Greg simply stopped to explain himself or ask for clarification.

articles.title: Brad Pitt Gives Promising Update on World War Z 2
articles.summary: Brad Pitt has given a promising update on the status of World War Z 2, a film that has been in development hell for over a decade.
articles.body:
Brad Pitt has given a promising update on the status of World War Z 2 , a film that has been in development hell for over a decade.

In 2013, Paramount released World War Z starring Brad Pitt, which became the highest-grossing zombie flick of all time. The movie itself wasn't anything to write home about, outside of a couple of cool action scenes, but it was a solid crowd-pleaser. And yet, Hollywood has been trying to crack the code on a follow-up for years. For a while, David Fincher was set to direct a sequel with Pitt returning , but that eventually fell apart. After that, it seemed like the project was dead.

However, as part of Skydance's new initiative to revitalize certain IP, leadership wants to prioritize a new World War Z film . When speaking with Collider , Pitt gave a small yet promising update on the film, which he believes could start shooting as soon as next year if they manage to lock down a script. He noted that they're "talking zombie logic" and polishing the script currently, trying to figure out a fresh angle on the genre.

"The thing is, it's well-worn territory," said Pitt in reference to zombie genre being somewhat saturated. "How do we keep it fresh? How do we take it somewhere it hasn't gone before? We've got some good ideas that I'm pretty excited about. We're fleshing them out now."

Should the film come to fruition, it will be directed by Edward Berger, who has directed acclaimed films such as Conclave and 2022's All Quiet on the Western Front. Pitt will also begin working on Ocean's 14 , the fourth film in the heist film franchise, sometime next year, as well.

Despite being 62 years old, Pitt clearly isn't backing down from his leading man role, particularly when it comes to intense and demanding action films like World War Z 2. As of right now, we'll just have to wait and see what happens. Does anyone really want a sequel to this movie 13 years later? It doesn't really seem like there's a flurry of demand for it, but at least the people behind the film seem passionate about it.

articles.title: GTA VI’s pretentious puzzler makes indie developers feel ‘part of larger culture’
articles.summary: Indie developers like Sam Barlow have commented on GTA VI’s Tenebrae Lux, which lampoons the genre, but also reflect on the impact of indie games on developers and mainstream culture.
articles.body: One of the most intriguing games of the year is called Tenebrae Lux. It’s a moody, black-and-white title with obtuse puzzles and a main character that constantly narrates to himself with dramatic language. Its credits attribute pretty much everything to a developer named Johannes Zuch. It’s generated a lot of discussion for seemingly mocking games like Jonathan Blow’s The Witness or The Chinese Room’s Dear Esther. It’s also a game that only exists inside of Grand Theft Auto VI. Developer Rockstar Games has stuffed a lot of satirical media inside of GTA VI, including TV shows you can watch, books you can read, and radio shows you can listen to. It’s all in service of making the world feel like a funhouse-mirror version of our current reality — Ted Lasso star Jason Sudeikis plays a right-wing radio host, for example. There are more games you can play inside GTA VI in addition to Tenebrae Lux, including a zombie-themed roguelike. But Tenebrae Lux, which you have to see as part of GTA VI’s main story, is the one that has struck a chord, including with indie developers like Sam Barlow and Robert Yang. [Image: “I have to admit it’s kind of funny for the biggest blockbuster game of all time to go after arthouse indie,” Yang tells The Verge, noting that it’s “like a fighter jet getting obsessed with an ant, petty in a funny way.” (Given that GTA VI earned $3.79 billion in its first day, the gulf between Rockstar and indie game studios that are struggling to get by is vast.) But Yang suggested that Rockstar developers are probably well versed in the types of games they’re lampooning in GTA VI. “I don’t think gamers understand how much indie experimental stuff any decent AAA dev plays,” Yang said, pointing out that Rockstar’s environmental artists and level designers “all probably love Dear Esther,” the influential first-person game that helped popularize the “walking sim” concept when it launched in 2012. “I was mostly taken with what it meant that the millions of people playing the game were having to sit down and play through an extended gag about indie games,” Barlow tells The Verge. “That made me feel like we were part of larger culture.” He added that he hopes some of these players might “seek out what these arty indie games might be.” Rockstar is self-aware enough to use its video games to poke fun at the medium itself. As part of a long conversation between protagonist Jason Duval and his friend Cal Hampton before they start playing Tenebrae Lux, Cal hypes the game by saying that none of it is “just sitting around waiting for people to finish talking.” Initially, you only play Tenebrae Lux for a few minutes, which is enough time to get stumped on the initial puzzles, before the game cuts back to Jason being bored. “Got anything else, a little less, uh… y’know?” he asks. They play the zombie game, titled Street Trash 3 Dezombifier, right after. (You can go back and play the entirety of Tenebrae Lux later if you want.) [Media: Barlow said that the cut “felt very true to the character and story. I gather there is more to the game, but it felt natural to me to hit a wall with the pretentious puzzle design and then move on!” Yang also pointed out that from a design perspective, GTA VI has more in common with Tenebrae Lux than Street Trash 3 Dezombifier. GTA VI is “basically a walking sim where you walk around Florida and listen to people talk,” Yang said. “What’s the difference? Well, just like a billion dollars I guess.”

articles.title: Players Have Found a GTA 6 60fps Glitch, but It Just Reaffirms Rockstar's 30fps Cap
articles.summary: One of GTA 6's biggest controversies was Rockstar's decision to keep the game's framerate locked at 30 fps, rather than allowing for an unlocked mode. Over the weekend, players managed to find a glitch on Xbox Series X that lets you unlock the frame rate, albeit to mixed results.
articles.body:
One of GTA 6 's biggest controversies was Rockstar's decision to keep the game's framerate locked at 30fps , rather than allowing for an unlocked mode. Over the weekend, players managed to find a glitch on Xbox Series X that lets you unlock the frame rate, albeit to mixed results.

The glitch is performed by booting up the game when the Xbox console is set to 60fps, then going into the console settings, switching the system to 120fps, launching another game, and then using Quick Resume to start GTA 6 back up. That process essentially tricks the system into unlocking the frame rate, and some people have been able to push it a bit higher than the game's default 30fps lock.

The folks over at Digital Foundry were able to put the '60fps glitch' to the test, though, and found that while you could push upwards of 60fps, it was limited to situations where, "If you look straight up in the ocean, frame-rates can just about graze 60fps."

Instead, Digital Foundry's results reaffirm Rockstar's decision to ship the game with a 30fps lock. While the game managed an average of 36fps in the first hour of the game, GTA 6 only gets more demanding as it progresses into Vice City, where NPCs and explosions are both more prevalent. And, in those situations, the game still has sharp drops to lower frame rates.

The whole reason a 30fps cap makes sense for GTA 6 is consistency. While this glitch shows that the game sometimes has the headroom to peek above 30fps, and even into the 40s, getting rid of the cap would just mean the difference between the peaks and valleys of the frame rate would be even higher, and thus more noticeable. It's no secret that the game does drop below 30 fps during heavy action or when you're speeding through the world, but any dip from 40fps to 24fps would be a lot more jarring than a dip from 30fps to 24fps.

This glitch has given some fans renewed hope that an unlocked version of the game would come out at some point, but Rockstar has been pretty clear about this generation's technical limitations. Right as GTA 6 was coming out, Rockstar technology production director Marc Chambers flat-out said that the PS5 Pro processor "is not powerful enough to run the game's complex simulation at higher frame rates." That's something I've noticed myself as I've started to cause more problems in Vice City.

Still, it would be nice to play GTA 6 at a higher frame rate, even if I have to wait for the PC version to do so. Luckily, it does seem like a PC port will be coming faster than previous entries , due to Rockstar's worry about an unofficial and AI-assisted port of the game. It's even starting to look like its fears on that front were justified .

articles.title: GTA 6's Waink App Can Unlock New Hairstyles and Makeup
articles.summary: You can use GTA 6's Waink app to scan specific magazines to unlock new hairstyles for Jason, as well as hair and makeup looks for Lucia.
articles.body:
We all know that finding magazines around Leonida is one of GTA's collectible quests , and we all know that the Waink app can be used to scan cars for information or street art. It turns out that it can also be used to scan specific magazines to unlock new hairstyles for Jason, as well as hair and makeup looks for Lucia — but these magazines are significantly harder to find.

I found one sitting by a chair in a random, but otherwise pretty boring part of Key Lento. It's not a magazine you can pick up and read like the collectible ones, but a scan with the Waink app unlocked a new Pop Star makeup style. It's apparently one of 15 "Lucia Magazine Styles" to unlock, and I imagine it's a similar number of facial hair and hair unlocks for Jason.

Rockstar has confirmed that additional hairstyles are available in GTA 6 , including those offered through the Vintage Vice City Pack, but it hasn’t published official instructions detailing how Waink’s hairstyle unlocks work. It's just another one of those fun little secrets that players have been left to find for themselves. So far I've only found one, but I'm now on a very serious hunt for the rest. The good news is that you do get a Waink prompt when you're close to one, so if you've been in any stores or locations wondering what the hell was setting it off, this might have been the answer.

This has now unlocked a whole new collectibles obsession for me, as if the books, magazines, collectible cars, birds, street art, and everything else you can find in our official guide weren't enough. This game will never let me know peace again.

articles.title: Ted Lasso Renewed for Season 5 on Apple TV
articles.summary: Ted Lasso is coming back to Apple TV for a fifth season, with production set to begin in April 2027.
articles.body:
Ted Lasso is coming back to Apple TV for a fifth season, with production set to begin in April 2027.

Apple TV’s beloved comedy series is coming back for another season, and it’s possible that there’s more in store. As pointed out by Variety , Jackson Sudeikis — who will return as both executive producer and star of the show — said he “would like to” continue the project through a sixth season in an October episode of Talk Easy with Sam Fragoso.

“Yeah, I just don’t know,” he told the host when asked about the topic, clarifying that he wasn’t holding anything back “intentionally.” “We haven’t started a writers’ room or anything like that,” he added.

For now, we know that Season 5 is in the bag, but this isn’t a huge surprise. In fact, it was almost a given, seeing how Season 4 was Apple TV’s biggest launch in the platform’s history. Its premiere garnered an astonishing 296.6 million minutes watched , proving the audience’s interest even after its initial storyline wrapped up at the end of Season 3.

Now, Ted’s on a new mission: to coach a women’s football team. The newly formed second-division team, the Lady Greyhounds, take Ted on a parallel journey with new obstacles, primarily navigating the environment of women’s athletics and the unique challenges that come with it.

Ted Lasso has been a hugely successful show, both among fans and critics alike. We at IGN scored its first season a glowing 9 out of 10 , calling it a “relentlessly optimistic and disarmingly charming comedy” that was sorely needed when it was released back in 2020. And while our review of the Season 4 premiere was comparatively softer , it certainly resonated with audiences enough to warrant a continuation of its new storyline.

For those who are unfamiliar with the show, it follows the kind, optimistic Ted Lasso, an American college football coach who gets hired to help a struggling English football league whose owner secretly hopes it fails. It’s a delightful watch, and a premise that has continued to prove sorely sought-after in the six years since its initial release.

Ted Lasso streams exclusively on Apple TV . For more shows streaming on the service, you can check out every series that’s making its way to the platform this November , which includes movies and shows like 12 12 12, Way of the Warrior Kid, and Stick Season 2.

articles.title: The hacker behind early GTA VI leaks has been sentenced — and released
articles.summary: Arion Kurtaj, who pleaded guilty to hacking Grand Theft Auto VI developer Rockstar Games and other companies, was sentenced to seven years in prison but released on license.
articles.body: Arion Kurtaj, who pleaded guilty last week to hacking Grand Theft Auto VI developer Rockstar Games and other companies, including Uber and Revolut, was sentenced to seven years in prison but released on license, the BBC reports. After hacking Rockstar, Kurtaj leaked 90 videos of GTA VI in 2022, years before the game’s public release last week. Prior to his sentencing, Kurtaj had already spent time in a hospital because of his autism and in prison. “You are obviously a very talented young man,” the judge in the case said, according to Sky News. “Don’t waste those talents by spending the rest of your life in and out of prison.” Kurtaj cannot use platforms Telegram and Discord as part of a five-year Serious Crime Prevention Order, the BBC says. Rockstar launched GTA VI last week to positive reviews. The studio said the game made $3.79 billion in its first day of sales.

articles.title: Here Are All of the Best Clips From the World's First Weekend With GTA 6
articles.summary: GTA 6 is here, and IGN has gathered all of the best (spoiler-free) clips from the world's first weekend with the game.
articles.body:
GTA 6 is here, and IGN has gathered all of the best (spoiler-free) clips from the world's first weekend with the game.

Rockstar Games are masters of crafting sandbox worlds for players to slam into, for better or worse. Alligators and bad drivers roam the streets of Leonida, so it's no surprise to see the early days of GTA 6 filled with slapstick moments that will live in everyone's heads for months to come.

The launch of GTA 6 marks a special moment for the gaming industry, and everyone's just trying to make the most of it. We could spend all day just watching the wackiest ways players have messed with the game's updated physics, but we did our best to put the highlights together for you here.

Lucia has more than earned her place in the history of the Grand Theft Auto franchise's history of protagonists. That hasn't stopped her from trying to show off if someone tries to pick a fight with Jason, though.

Find yourself a girl like Lucia man. Kicked him so hard she fell to the ground too 🤣 — chaotic memes (@memechaotic) November 23, 2026

Find yourself a girl like Lucia man. Kicked him so hard she fell to the ground too 🤣

You can do just about anything in GTA 6. You can help your friend get something to drink, rob drug dealers, go for late-night drives, and you can even wake up every morning and steal your neighbor's propane tank.

This is genuinely killing me LMAOOO — Lexi (@original_lexi) November 23, 2026

So much of what happens in GTA 6 is in the player's control… but there's a lot that isn't, too.

Unluckiest GTA 6 player by far, hit by a random traffic barrier launched by a passing car. — GTA 6 Countdown ⏳ (@GTAVI_Countdown) November 22, 2026

Unluckiest GTA 6 player by far, hit by a random traffic barrier launched by a passing car.

We'll probably be learning about all the different ways players can beat up Leonida citizens for years. Today, WWE watchers can rest easy knowing Jason is a Sheamus fan.

THE SHEAMUS BROGUE KICK HAS MADE IT INTO GTA 6 😭 — FADE (@FadeAwayMedia) November 23, 2026

THE SHEAMUS BROGUE KICK HAS MADE IT INTO GTA 6 😭

Look, we're all going to have to get used to GTA 6 being the internet's new clip generator, but that doesn't mean every video that comes out of Rockstar's latest has to be part of one big gag. Players have already found some amazing things that they can do in the game, including X/Twitter user @perrikaryal, who managed to steal a fighter plane with nothing but her mind.

I STOLE A JET WITH MIND CONTROL IN GTA6 this took me AGES you have no idea what should I do next?? This electroencephalogram (EEG) records my brain activity and when I'm imagining something I've trained the software to recognise (like pushing a cube forward), a button will be pressed on my virtual xbox controller. For this run, I was imagining pushing a boulder to accelerate, getting angry to interact with vehicles, and imagining a cricket hopping to jump. I use eyetracking and gyro for joysticks :) — Perri (@perrikaryal) November 22, 2026

I STOLE A JET WITH MIND CONTROL IN GTA6 this took me AGES you have no idea what should I do next?? This electroencephalogram (EEG) records my brain activity and when I'm imagining something I've trained the software to recognise (like pushing a cube forward), a button will be pressed on my virtual xbox controller. For this run, I was imagining pushing a boulder to accelerate, getting angry to interact with vehicles, and imagining a cricket hopping to jump. I use eyetracking and gyro for joysticks :)

Another incredible story that IGN reported on recently saw one Neuralink participant using the technology to launch into the opening moments of the game's story. You can see what that experience was like for them below.

Playing GTA VI with a Neuralink — Neuralink (@neuralink) November 20, 2026

Leonida's Wildlife Is More Than Just a Few Cute Critters

You're probably aware that Florida served as the main inspiration for everything from Vice City's streets to its musty swamps. That's why alligators are so easy to find, and while they're always looking for something to eat, Jason and Lucia don't necessarily have to be on the menu.

primeira pessoa do mundo a fazer 67 no gta 6 — yaskis (@teenidl3kin) November 20, 2026

primeira pessoa do mundo a fazer 67 no gta 6

For as much as it has going on, GTA 6 is surprisingly polished. Does Rockstar still have scratches to buff out? Well, maybe.

Relatable walk off after a massive and painful accident #GTA6 — GTA 6 Clips (@GtaGameClips) November 23, 2026

Relatable walk off after a massive and painful accident #GTA6

Some of the best clips from GTA 6's first weekend in the world's hands came from players just experimenting with its world. For example, X user @NotForYouIn showcased an interesting use for gasoline.

Fire Physics in GTA 6 🔥 — Not For You (@NotForYouIN) November 23, 2026

This one comes from Twitch streamer Develique and shows just how...unpredictable the world of GTA 6 can be. Even stopping to show a little dog friend some love may not pan out the way you expected.

'GTA 6' is already Creating some of the most LEGENDARY CLIPS yet — chumBucket (@ChumBucketDrama) November 18, 2026

'GTA 6' is already Creating some of the most LEGENDARY CLIPS yet

Why Drive a Full Car When Half a Car Does the Trick?

We uh… probably don't need to say much about this one.

GTA 6 got no respect for personal property. Bro just opens the door and takes your car. 💀 — Sinister (@SinisterX010) November 23, 2026

GTA 6 got no respect for personal property. Bro just opens the door and takes your car. 💀

Jason and Lucia are the stars of GTA 6. Sometimes, though, the main characters are the NPCs.

Didn't expect that 😭 — GTAClipper.com (@GTAClipperLive) November 23, 2026

Hundreds of clips have been published in the short amount of time the public has had its hands on GTA 6. The one we've seen shared around most, though, is a simple but effective gag that, unfortunately for Jason, looks like something out of Looney Tunes.

This is the funniest GTA 6 clip I’ve seen so far 🤣 — GameVerse 🎮 (@TheGameVerse) November 21, 2026

This is the funniest GTA 6 clip I’ve seen so far 🤣

Have you ever seen the Wile E. Coyote bit where he paints a tunnel on the side of a wall before later running into it himself? Rockstar has, too .

OK, so the alligators can be friendly, but what about the sharks? Well…

“Do you hear that music? Why does it sound so ominous?” Famous last words😭😭😭😭 — bella 𓏲 ࣪₊♡𓂃 (@flattenmydays) November 20, 2026

“Do you hear that music? Why does it sound so ominous?” Famous last words😭😭😭😭

GTA 6's cow kill count will probably always be low, but it will never be zero.

The stupidest death in GTA VI so far — VideoArtGame (@VideoArtGame) November 20, 2026

Planes, trains, and automobiles; GTA 6 has it all. One of the best parts of Leonida, though, is its wide-open waters and the many ways Jason and Lucia can use the sea for travel. However, with a bit of experimenting, it looks like you can take Jason's kayak just about anywhere.

😂😂😂😂 — مشعل (@MG4MER3) November 23, 2026

GTA 6's first weekend was filled with memes and unforgettable clips, but after reviews quickly painted it as the highest-rated game of all time , that probably isn't too surprising. IGN gave it a 10/10 , too, calling it "exquisitely detailed, endlessly ripe for experimentation, and uncompromisingly engineered."

Just getting started in GTA 6 or wondering what to do next? Check out the Official Grand Theft Auto 6 guide right here on IGN. If you're still getting your bearings, discover GTA's new systems with the Beginner's Guide - 67 Tips and Tricks , or get all the details on the first chapters with the Chapter 1 Guide and Tips , Chapter 2 Guide and Tips , and Chapter 3 Guide and Tips . If you're already driving all around Leonida and want to know everything there is to find and do, see the Leonida interactive map .

We almost certainly missed other funny and interesting clips from the weekend. Be sure to tell us about your favorites in the comments below!

Michael Cripe is a freelance writer with IGN. He's best known for his work at sites like The Pitch, The Escapist, and OnlySP. Be sure to give him a follow on Bluesky (@mikecripe.bsky.social) and Twitter (@MikeCripe).

A Brother Once More is an optional Tale side quest in Phantom Blade Zero . Started in Pangzhen, to begin this quest you will need the Haung Manor Key.

This can be found from Shopkeeper Niu inside Myst's tavern, a key story location in Pangzhen. Once there, head into the Haung Manor and to the top floor. Here you can find a Memory Flower, which when picked up begins the quest.

articles.body:
There are X Memory Flowers in Mirage Estate. Check the map above for their general location and the rest of the guide for the individual spots.

Shortly after you enter Mirage Estate and find the first bell, Estate Rear Gate, you’ll have to open a door. Past it, you’ll find the first flower inside a temple in front of you, with a spirit talking. You’ll have to defeat a new type of enemy before you can pick up the flower.

This is Yu’er’s Memory Flower I - Struggle.

As you move past the previous area, you’ll see a temple on your right, while the main path continues on the left. Enter the former temple and fight three puppets. The flower will be on the table in the center.

This is Patron Gao’s Memory Flower I - Thread-Binding Sect.
